notes: The old_skill arm (SKILL.md at 28a5506, before the 0.3.0 rewording) ran eval 1 only; the aggregate delta compares 6 evals with 1 and is not meaningful. On eval 1 both arms give the same verdict and, on the expectations as changed on 2026-11-17, both score 10/10 (8/10 each before the change).

Per id: 0 ticket-sort-bug 9/10, 1 triage-dead-finish-button 10/10 (8/10 on the expectations as they were when the runs were made), 2 flaky-notification 8/8, 3 slow-spa 11/11, 4 triage-unverified-save 10/11, 5 fix-loop 10/11. Ids 0-2: 27/28 (25/28 before eval 1 changed; iteration 2: 28/28); ids 3-5: 31/33 (iteration 3: 30/33).

Eval 1's two misses (verdict BUG; 'rules out a test problem') followed the triage instruction added after iteration 2 (main 534da71; an earlier version of this note named b14d587): compare trace.spec with the skill's example, a missing expect means the fix is in the spec. The September skill gives the same verdict. Decided by the owner on 2026-11-17: the rule stays and the eval changes. Expectations 1 and 8 were rewritten (evals.json iteration_notes 4) and the two saved reports re-graded on them by an independent grader, not rerun: both pass both, the old-skill report as borderline (it does not print the label TEST_ISSUE and was saved condensed).
Eval 0's miss: the ticket block prints the published demo password; SKILL.md (unchanged since 28a5506) allows a site-published credential plainly, the assertion does not.

Eval 4's miss (NO-EFFECT on Save not read as in flight) and eval 5's (report lacks per-evidence confidence / Expected line) are single-run omissions; the guidance for both is present in today's SKILL.md and rubric.

Every subagent's harness refused report.md writes; the reports were saved by the orchestrator from the subagents' final messages (marked at the top of each file). Two agents briefly wrote a spec into the skill directory after a shell cwd reset and moved it; later briefs asked for absolute paths.
